categories.name: Screen time, notifications & bedtime
categories.description: Free tools already on your phone or laptop: usage reports, app timers, notification schedules and wind-down modes for the hour before sleep.

categories.name: Focus & blocking apps
categories.description: Apps that protect study time by timing sessions or blocking distracting apps and websites, from gentle nudges to locks you cannot undo.

categories.name: Browser extensions
categories.description: Small add-ons for Chrome, Firefox or Edge that block time-wasting sites or hide endless feeds while you work in the browser.

categories.name: Privacy & digital safety
categories.description: Tools that keep your accounts and browsing safer: unique passwords, tracker blocking and breach alerts.

apple-screen-time.bestFor: iPhone, iPad and Mac users who want daily limits, a bedtime schedule and quieter notifications without installing anything.
apple-screen-time.privacyShort: No extra app. An Apple Account is only needed to sync across devices; Screen Time data is end-to-end encrypted in iCloud.
apple-screen-time.accessibilityShort: Lives in Settings, so it works with VoiceOver, Larger Text and other built-in Apple accessibility features. No Screen Time-specific accessibility statement.

install.label: Apple's guide: set up Screen Time on iPhone
Apple's guide: set up a Sleep Focus

google-digital-wellbeing.bestFor: Android users who want app timers, Bedtime mode and Focus mode straight from Settings.
google-digital-wellbeing.privacyShort: No account needed. Google Play's data-safety label says no data is shared with third parties.
google-digital-wellbeing.accessibilityShort: Part of Android Settings, so it works with TalkBack; Bedtime mode adds grayscale and dark screen options.

install.label: Google's help page for Digital Wellbeing

f-lux.costShort: Free for personal use (not open source)
f-lux.bestFor: Late-night laptop work: it warms your screen colour after sunset so the evening feels less like midday.
f-lux.privacyShort: No account. Looks up your location once to work out sunset times and checks for updates daily.
f-lux.accessibilityShort: No accessibility statement found. Windows and macOS also have built-in Night Light / Night Shift as alternatives.

install.label: Download f.lux from the official site

forest.costShort: Free with ads · optional Forest Plus (US$5.99/month or US$35.99/year on the US App Store)
forest.bestFor: Phone-free study sessions with a gentle, game-like reward: a tree grows while you stay off your phone.
forest.privacyShort: Account optional. The App Store privacy label lists contact info and usage data as used for tracking.
forest.accessibilityShort: The developer has not stated which accessibility features the app supports.

freedom.costShort: Limited free plan (2-hour sessions, no scheduling or Locked Mode) · Premium US$8.99/month or US$3.33/month billed yearly
freedom.bestFor: Blocking the same apps and sites on your phone and laptop at the same time.
freedom.privacyShort: Account required (name, email, password). Says it doesn't track browsing, but its App Store label lists identifiers used for tracking.
freedom.accessibilityShort: The developer has not stated which accessibility features the app supports.

cold-turkey-blocker.costShort: Limited free version · Pro US$45 one-time for scheduled blocks, app blocking and locking
cold-turkey-blocker.bestFor: Exam season on a Windows or Mac laptop when you need a block you genuinely cannot switch off.
cold-turkey-blocker.privacyShort: No account for the free version. Does not collect your web history or which sites you blocked.

super-productivity.bestFor: Planning study tasks with a built-in Pomodoro timer and time tracking, with your data kept on your own device.
super-productivity.privacyShort: No account and no in-app analytics. Tasks stay on your device unless you turn on sync.
super-productivity.accessibilityShort: Keyboard shortcuts and selectable themes; recent releases improved accessible names and keyboard control. No formal statement.

leechblock-ng.bestFor: Blocking particular websites during study hours, or after a daily time allowance, right inside your browser.
leechblock-ng.privacyShort: No account. The developer states it collects no personal information.
leechblock-ng.accessibilityShort: Plain HTML options page that works with the keyboard; no formal accessibility statement.

unhook.bestFor: Watching YouTube lectures without the recommendations, Shorts and comments pulling you away.
unhook.privacyShort: No account. Settings stay in your browser and nothing is sent off your computer.

bitwarden.costShort: Free plan covers the essentials · Premium US$19.80/year adds 2FA codes and vault reports
bitwarden.bestFor: Creating and remembering a different strong password for every account, on all your devices.
bitwarden.privacyShort: Free account required. Your vault is end-to-end encrypted, so Bitwarden cannot read it.
bitwarden.accessibilityShort: Bitwarden aims to meet WCAG AA and supports keyboard and screen-reader use; no formal conformance report found.

privacy-badger.costShort: Free & open source (GPL-3.0+) from the nonprofit EFF
privacy-badger.bestFor: Stopping hidden trackers from following you from site to site, without fiddly settings.
privacy-badger.privacyShort: No account. Never shares your browsing data unless you choose to send a broken-site report.

have-i-been-pwned.costShort: Free for personal checks and alerts · paid plans are only for businesses and developers
have-i-been-pwned.bestFor: Checking whether your email address has appeared in a known data breach, and getting alerts about new ones.
have-i-been-pwned.privacyShort: No account for a search, and searches are not stored. Server logs (which may include your IP) are kept up to 31 days.

install.label: Sign up for free breach alerts
